title: ETBUS vs. Non-ETBUS: How Non-US Residents Running a US LLC Actually Determine Their US Tax Liability in 2026
content:
# ETBUS vs. Non-ETBUS: How Non-US Residents Running a US LLC Actually Determine Their US Tax Liability in 2026

Most guides skip the part that actually matters: whether you owe US tax at all depends on a single determination most people never make correctly. If you run a US LLC as a non-resident, you are either Engaged in a US Trade or Business (ETBUS) or you are not. That distinction controls everything.

---

## What ETBUS Actually Means

The IRS does not publish a clean checklist for ETBUS status. It is determined by facts and circumstances, but two factors carry the most weight.

**Dependent Agent:** Do you have a person in the United States who is not an independent contractor, who habitually exercises authority to conclude contracts on your behalf? If yes, you are almost certainly ETBUS.

**Regular, Continuous, and Considerable Activity:** Is your business activity in the US systematic and ongoing, not isolated or sporadic? A one-off US client does not make you ETBUS. A consistent, recurring pattern of serving US customers from US infrastructure likely does.

> **Note:** Your LLC being registered in the US does not automatically make you ETBUS. Formation state and physical business activity are two completely separate things.

---

## The Non-ETBUS Path: What It Means for Your Taxes

If you are Non-ETBUS, your single-member LLC (treated as a disregarded entity) produces income that is not subject to US federal income tax, provided that income is not:

- **Fixed, Determinable, Annual, or Periodical (FDAP) income** sourced in the US (think royalties, interest, dividends, or rents from US sources)
- **Effectively Connected Income (ECI)** from a US trade or business

For most non-resident digital entrepreneurs running a service-based LLC with no US employees, no US office, and no dependent US agent, the income flows through to the foreign owner and is taxed only in their home country (or not at all, depending on their tax residency situation).

The LLC still has potential filing obligations. Form 5472 paired with Form 1120 (pro forma) is required annually if your disregarded LLC had any reportable transactions with related parties, including you funding or withdrawing from the business.

> **Note:** Skipping Form 5472 is one of the most expensive mistakes non-resident LLC owners make. The penalty starts at $25,000 per violation.

---

## The ETBUS Path: What You Actually Owe

If you are ETBUS, your income becomes Effectively Connected Income and is taxed at the same graduated federal rates that apply to US residents. The 2026 brackets for single filers, adjusted for inflation, are:

| Taxable Income (2026, Single Filer) | Federal Rate |
|---|---|
| Up to $12,400 | 10% |
| $12,401 to $50,400 | 12% |
| $50,401 to $103,350 | 22% |
| $103,351 to $197,300 | 24% |
| Above $197,300 | 32% to 37% |

You would also need to file Form 1040-NR and potentially pay self-employment tax, state income tax (depending on your LLC's formation and nexus state), and comply with quarterly estimated tax payments.

---

## The Three Factors That Push You Into ETBUS Territory

Most non-residents drift into ETBUS without realising it. Watch for these:

1. **Hiring a US-based employee or dedicated agent.** Even a part-time VA in Texas who signs proposals or books clients on your behalf can create ETBUS status.
2. **Leasing US office space or a co-working membership in your company name.** A fixed place of business in the US is a textbook ETBUS indicator.
3. **Performing services personally while inside the US.** If you travel to the US and perform billable work for clients during that trip, those earnings are likely ECI, even if the rest of your income is not.

---

## Where Tax Treaties Come In

The US has income tax treaties with dozens of countries. If your home country has a treaty with the US, those treaties may reduce or eliminate FDAP withholding rates and can sometimes affect ETBUS determinations for residents of treaty countries.

The critical step is checking whether your country of tax residency has a treaty and what the specific business profits article says. Treaties vary significantly. Do not assume.

---

## Practical Steps to Take Right Now

- Audit your current operations against the ETBUS criteria above
- Confirm whether your LLC had reportable transactions requiring Form 5472
- Check the US tax treaty status for your country of tax residency
- Consult a US tax professional who works specifically with non-resident LLC owners (this is a specialist area, not a general CPA topic)

> **Note:** This post is educational and does not constitute tax or legal advice. Your specific situation requires a qualified professional review.
